notes: pandapaxxy (PvE / M+KB / Controller): "False Promises is a returning auto rifle from yesteryear. It's a High-Impact frame with decent handling but pretty poor stability. There's not a lot you can do to improve that outside of directly investing or giving up a perk like Feeding Frenzy for Dynamic Sway Reduction. I wouldn't advise it unless you have a really hard time controlling the recoil. Cascade Point and Headseeker provide alternating utility through increasing rpm without a damage penalty or Stasis synergy. Depending on your build I'd personally go with Cascade Point because it feels more fun." Recommended MW: Reload Speed.

pandapaxxy (PvP / Controller): "Over in PvP False Promises has a bit more of a leg up. High damage per shot paired with a high range stat will cover most maps outside of scout rifle ranges. Cascade Point shows up here again as the firing delay is a whopping 40% dropping the time to kill from 0.83s to 0.50s. The requirements for a kill don't change at 6c but being far faster will catch people by surprise." Recommended MW: Stability.

[YeezyGT's S15] (PvE): [MW: Stability / Reload Speed] "False Promises is a late bloomer. Four seasons later, with Anti-Barrier Auto Rifle being the [only] AB mod, 360RPMs have the blend of range + damage potential that's needed for high-level content to occupy the space usually reserved for Scout Rifles. You're unlikely to need an additional Range bump - invest in Stability to allow for consistent shooting, and False Promises is blessed with a good stock recoil direction as-is. I feel as though Rampage isn't a huge help, given the slow time-to-kill on 360RPMs and short Rampage duration (3s), though would hold onto a roll anyway."

I've been waiting for a Legendary High-Impact AR that felt like SUROS Regime with Dual Speed Receiver, and I think we've finally found one. Stat-wise it suffers from most of the same drawbacks that the other high impacts do, poor stability, low aim assist and handling, but for some reason the return to center speed of the reticle is much faster than I'm used to on the others guns in the archetype (like Halfdan) and so the low stability doesn't seem to have much of an effect of the usability of the weapon."
